instructions: Courtly is an iOS app (SwiftUI, iOS 17+) with a Supabase backend (Postgres with PostGIS, row-level security, security-definer SQL functions, Deno Edge Functions) and a static policy site. The iOS app talks to the backend only through the typed wrappers in ios/Courtly/Services/API.swift, which call database functions by name. Review for correctness, security and privacy first; style comments are off. When a change touches both the app and the SQL, check that the JSON shapes, parameter names and raised error codes still agree.

rules.rule: Every new or renamed function in schema public that the app must call needs an explicit `grant execute ... to authenticated` in the same migration (see supabase/migrations/0009_function_grants.sql). Never add a blanket `grant execute on all functions`. Internal helpers (JSON builders, predicates, writers) must not be granted; flag any helper that takes an arbitrary user id or chat id and is reachable over the API.

Migration files that have already been deployed must not be modified in place; the deploy script skips files recorded as applied. Put changes to existing functions or tables in a new, higher-numbered migration.

Functions declared `security definer` must set `search_path`, must start by resolving the caller (assert_signed_in or assert_onboarded) and must check visibility themselves (can_see_hit, is_chat_member, is_hit_host). Lock the hit row before its request or invite row, the order add_player uses, to avoid deadlocks.

Errors raised for the app must be short snake_case codes (`raise exception 'hit_full'`). A new code needs a matching entry in ios/Courtly/Services/Supabase/BackendMessages.swift, and the smoke test in supabase/tests/smoke.sql should cover new functions and new failure paths.

Never store or send a precise coordinate: locations are a ZIP or city centroid (LocationService.coarsened). Contact hashes are computed server-side from verified values; the client must not write phone_hash or email_hash. Anything shown to other players goes through player_card, never profile_json.

Do not turn a failed network call into an empty state with `try?`. Keep the error (an ErrorCaption, a QuietCard with the message, or the store's error field) so offline is distinguishable from 'nothing here'.

Services held by a SwiftUI View (CalendarService, LocationService, PlaceSearchCompleter, EKEventStore) must be `@State` or live in an @Observable store, never a plain stored `let`, because the struct is rebuilt on every render.
Contacts enumeration, HMAC hashing, image decoding and downscaling must run off the main actor (Task.detached) and only assign results on the main actor.

Calendar dates such as birthdays are formatted and parsed in the device time zone as yyyy-MM-dd, never through a GMT formatter. Any `ClosedRange<Date>` built from user input must guarantee lowerBound <= upperBound, since the `...` operator traps otherwise.

Anything that holds per-user state outside SwiftUI (RealtimeHub channels, SnapshotCache, ProfileCache, the app badge, DeepLinkCenter.pending, the stored APNs token) must be cleared in AppSession.signOut() and deleteAccount().

Workflows must read tokens only from repository secrets, never from workflow_dispatch inputs. The deploy must never regenerate a secret the Edge Functions also hold unless it updates both in the same step.

Statements on the policy, terms and support pages must match what the backend does: what is stored (own email and phone hashes, weekly busy flags), retention periods, what blocking hides, and how deletion works. Flag any new claim the code does not implement.
